heading: Key Concepts
content: Cost Price (CP) is the price at which an article is purchased.
Selling Price (SP) is the price at which an article is sold.
Marked Price (MP) is the price printed on the product before any discount.
Profit occurs when the selling price is greater than the cost price.
Loss occurs when the selling price is less than the cost price.
Profit percentage and loss percentage are generally calculated on the cost price unless mentioned otherwise.
Discount is always calculated on the marked price.
Successive discounts cannot be added directly. Use the equivalent discount formula.
For equal gain and equal loss percentages on two articles sold at the same selling price, the overall result is always a loss.
In false-weight or dishonest-dealer questions, profit comes from supplying less quantity while charging for the full quantity.
Always identify whether the percentage is based on Cost Price, Selling Price, or Marked Price before applying any formula.
Placement questions often combine profit, discount, markup and false-weight concepts in a single problem.
